title: sagraea coriacea
intro: Sagraea coriacea, commonly known as "Wild Potato" or "Wild Sweet Potato," is a perennial plant species native to the tropical forests of Central and South America. It is known for its edible tubers, which are rich in nutrients and offer various health benefits, including antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, which can help manage conditions such as arthritis and diabetes. The plant's therapeutic actions include its ability to stimulate digestion, reduce fever, and alleviate respiratory issues. Sagraea coriacea contains bioactive constituents like flavonoids, alkaloids, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential uses in traditional medicine.
